author: Apocali
quote:
This game should not be called GTA.

GTA is more than just a title. It's a promise of a certain experience: a satirical criminal underworld filled with dark humor, morally dysfunctional antiheroes, and the freedom for players to explore the sandbox on their own terms. This identity was established and refined over decades, largely thanks to the legendary Dan Houser.

GTA VI, however, was written under different creative leadership.

What I find particularly disturbing is Rob Nelson's interview with The Guardian (November 15, 2026), where he discusses deliberately encouraging different player behavior through gameplay mechanics. From a player's perspective, this can easily feel like an attempt to impose the developers' own values rather than preserve the freedom that has always defined GTA.

Technically and graphically, GTA VI is an absolute marvel. But when the creative leadership prioritizes pushing a particular message over respecting the established identity of the franchise..

After 13 years of waiting, I feel robbed.
